rows.note: Use this all-purpose spoken phrasing when saying what people ordinarily call something rather than its official name.

example.english: People colloquially call this place Tai Hang, but fewer people know its official name.
example.traditional: 呢個地方平時叫做大坑，正式名就冇咁多人識。
example.jyutping: nei1 go3 dei6 fong1 ping4 si4 giu3 zou6 daai6 haang1 zing3 sik1 ming4 zau6 mou5 gam3 do1 jan4 sik1

rows.note: Use this when explicitly contrasting a colloquial spoken form with a formal or written one.

example.english: Colloquially, we say “Have you eaten?” but we would not write it that way.
example.traditional: 口語上，我哋會講「食咗飯未」，書面語就唔會咁寫。
example.jyutping: hau2 jyu5 soeng6 ngo5 dei6 wui5 gong2 sik6 zo2 faan6 mei6 syu1 min6 jyu5 zau6 m4 wui5 gam3 se2

rows.note: Use this mainly for a common or informal name, especially when introducing what something is commonly called.

example.english: This illness is colloquially known as a cold, while its medical name is much more complicated.
example.traditional: 呢種病俗稱傷風，醫學名就複雜得多。
example.jyutping: ne1 zung2 beng6 zuk6 cing1 soeng1 fung1 ji1 hok6 ming4 zau6 fuk1 zaap6 dak1 do1
